howDoI.q: How do I draw a room that looks as if it is seen from a corner?
How do I make a cube that has a top and two sides?
How do I make a wall that runs on a slant?
How do I draw a tower that is taller than one block?
How do I make steps that look as if they climb?
How do I make an arrow key walk on a slant?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Corner View is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has three short rooms, all drawn as if you were looking at them from one corner: a floor of diamonds, cubes with a top and two sides, a stair of towers and a floor shaped like a diamond. It takes a few minutes to finish.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each idea is made.

The keys

The four arrows walk Lena: the squares in the first two rooms, the diagonals in the third. Space does nothing. Walk onto the gold diamond to go on. Nothing in this game hurts Lena.

pages.head: Level 1: The Corner Room
pages.html:
Level 1: The Corner Room

Lena starts on the green diamond in the middle of a room of cubes. The DIAMOND FLOOR, SQUARE GRID sign says what this is: the floor is drawn in diamonds, but the game under it is still squares. The A CUBE IS ONE BLOCK sign points at the cubes: each one is a diamond top and two sides, in a single 20 by 20 block.

A wall of cubes climbs to the right, like a wall seen from a corner. Walk straight at it and Lena is stopped. The ARROWS WALK THE SQUARES sign says why: here each arrow is one straight square step, even though Lena is drawn facing a diagonal. Level 3 shows how to make a diagonal step. They go up one, right one, up one, right one, round the open top end of the wall, and down to the gold diamond.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • One picture, cut into blocks. The floor, the cubes, the signs' posts and the two diamonds were painted as one 320 by 200 picture and cut into 20 by 20 blocks. Open one.bbl in the blocks editor to see them. The floor's diamonds repeat every 20 pixels, so every plain floor cell comes out as the same block, which is why a whole room needs few blocks.
  • A cube is one block. A cube is 20 pixels wide and 20 tall: a diamond top, a left side in a darker color and a right side darker still. The cube blocks have Solid sides checked, so Lena cannot walk through them. Their four corners show the floor.
  • The wall that runs on a slant. Open one.map in the map editor. The wall is cubes in cells that touch only at their corners, one row up and one column right each time. Lena moves a whole block at a time along the squares, so they cannot slip between two cubes that only touch at a corner. They go up, then right, then up, then right.
  • The walls round the room. A ring of purple cubes closes the room in, and the whole map outside it is the same cube, so they never stops at something they cannot see.
  • Lena's place. They start in the middle of the screen on purpose: the view is fixed, and the game centers it on where they start. Open cv.gam in the scenes editor: its scroll settings are all off, so the picture stays put.
  • Lena in a corner view. Open square.chr in the character editor. Every block in this game has Gravity pulls unchecked, and Lena has four walks and no jump. Their pictures (kit.cbl) face only the four diagonals, as a person seen from a corner, never the camera: facing front they would look wider than they are tall. Here each arrow still walks one square step, so Up faces upper right while moving straight up. Level 3 fixes that.

What it cannot do. A corner view is a picture, not a 3D room. The game cannot sort what is in front from what is behind, so Lena is always drawn on top of everything: they cannot walk behind a cube or a tower. And their moves stay square: in these two rooms they cannot walk along the drawn diagonal, only up, down, left and right. Level 3 does.

pages.head: Level 2: Stairs of Towers
pages.html:
Level 2: Stairs of Towers

Lena starts on the green diamond in the middle again, and the gold diamond is on the far side of a stair of five towers: one, two and three blocks tall, and back down. The TALL TOWERS COVER THE BLOCKS ABOVE THEM sign says what a tall tower is: its picture covers the block above the one it stands on, so that block is solid too.

Walk left and the stair stops them. Go right past its end, down, along the front and up to the gold diamond. The LENA IS ALWAYS IN FRONT sign is about them: they are drawn over everything, so they never goes behind a tower.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • A tall tower is more than one block. A cube is 20 pixels tall. A tower that rises further is a taller picture: the top diamond sits in the block above the one it stands on. Open two.bbl: the three-block tower is the top, the middle and the bottom blocks of one painting, and each has Solid sides checked. The blocks above a tower's foot are solid too, because the tower's picture is drawn there and Lena should not be able to stand on it.
  • The stair is only a picture. The towers are one, two and three blocks tall, lined up in a row, so they look like steps. Lena does not climb them: they are walls, and they walk round them.
  • Lena is in front. The game draws Lena over every block. A game that sorts by depth would draw a tower over them when they walk behind it. Here the picture would have to be changed by hand: each tower would need a second set of blocks, put in place when Lena passes. That is a good next step to try.

What it cannot do. There is no real depth sorting, and Lena's walks stay square here. Everything else is the same game as level 1.

pages.head: Level 3: The Diamond Floor
pages.html:
Level 3: The Diamond Floor

The room is a diamond, and every arrow walks along one of its edges. Lena is drawn facing the way they walk, always one of the four slants and never the camera. Four signs in the dark corners say which arrow goes where: UP IS UPPER RIGHT, RIGHT IS LOWER RIGHT, DOWN IS LOWER LEFT, LEFT IS UPPER LEFT. The EACH ARROW TAKES THE NEAREST SLANT sign says why this fits: Up and Right lean toward the top and the right of the screen, so they take the slants nearest them, and the other two follow around.

To go straight right or left, tap two arrows in turn: Left, then Down, again and again, makes a straight line left; Up, then Right, makes one to the right. Walk into the lower right wall with Right, then hold Up all the way to the gold diamond.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 3 is made

  • A step that moves both ways. Open diag.chr in the character editor and look at the Up sequence. Each frame has an X of 4 and a Y of -2: the engine adds both to their place on every frame, so one key walks a slant. The floor's diamonds are twice as wide as tall, so a step along their edge is 4 across and 2 up or down. square.chr, used in levels 1 and 2, has an X or a Y but never both.
  • The same pictures. Both character files use kit.cbl: four slants, three poses each (a step, standing, the other step). The left-hand ones are the right-hand ones mirrored.
  • Which arrow goes where. Up is upper right, Right is lower right, Down is lower left and Left is upper left: each arrow takes the slant nearest its own direction, going around clockwise, so the four still feel like the four arrows. A sequence is tied to a key, so you can pick any mapping.
  • A wall on a slant. Open three.map. The diamond's edges are cubes in steps of two blocks across and one down, the slope Lena walks. The blocks outside them are dark and solid. The engine moves them across, then down, and stops each at a solid block, so they glide along a slanted wall instead of sticking in it.

What it cannot do. Lena's box is still a square block, so their edges do not follow the diamond: they slide along a slanted wall in tiny steps, and they cannot stand on a diamond tile's exact corner. Straight up, down, left and right take two arrows in turn. Each level has one character file, so the arrows mean the same thing all through a level.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • In one.map, move a cube of the wall one block and see where Lena can go.
  • Open a cube block in one.bbl and uncheck Solid sides: Lena walks right through the cube, drawn under them.
  • Change the colors of a cube's sides in the blocks editor.
  • Draw a new cube in a free block and put it in the map.

The home page’s Starters tab has more small games like this one.

box.back: A small explorer in a red beanie crosses three rooms drawn from a corner: a floor of diamonds, cubes with tops and sides, a stair of towers, a floor shaped like a diamond. It is one painting cut into square blocks, so in the first two rooms they walk the squares, not the diamonds, and in the third each arrow walks a diagonal. Read the signs, then open the game in Game-Maker and look at the blocks.
features: A floor of diamonds and cubes, drawn on the square grid
Lena walks the four arrow ways round a diagonal wall, then the four diagonals
Made to be copied and taken apart

blurb: Three rooms drawn as if seen from one corner: a floor of diamonds, cubes with a top and two sides, a stair of towers and a diamond-shaped floor. It is all pictures cut into square blocks, so in the first two rooms Lena walks on the squares and goes round the diagonal wall in square steps. In the third their arrows each walk one diagonal of the floor, the way the room is laid out. Signs say how. Play it, then open it in Game-Maker and look at the blocks.

72.long: Walk up the screen in levels 1 and 2. In level 3 it walks up and to the right.

75.long: Walk left on the squares in levels 1 and 2. In level 3 it walks up and to the left, along one diagonal of the floor.

77.long: Walk right on the squares in levels 1 and 2. In level 3 it walks down and to the right.

80.long: Walk down the screen in levels 1 and 2. In level 3 it walks down and to the left.
